summary: Instagram is where the audience is: almost every video there gets 400 to 1,400 views, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best videos use a 'sensor doesn't do what you think' hook on familiar gadgets or robots (gyro robot, clap switch, line follower), and they earn likes, saves and shares. Weak spots are generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai?' questions, which got almost nothing, and videos not posted to Instagram at all (the early October batch).
winningPattern: Short, myth-busting Hindi titles in the form 'X doesn't do [obvious thing], it only does [surprising thing]' or 'Without X this robot falls', about relatable gadgets and robots (gyro, clap switch, line follower, DHT11, mic). Posted on Instagram Reels, with a single emoji and #shorts. Saves come from robot/maker demos, and shares come from surprising everyday-life facts like UV through clouds and soil sensors.
doMore: Post every video to Instagram first, since it delivers 10 to 50 times the views of YouTube for this channel
Use the 'doesn't X, only Y' myth-bust title with a visible consequence (robot falls, switch triggers wrongly)
Make robot and maker-project demos (gyro, clap switch, line follower), which earn the most saves
Add a 'send this to a friend' angle to everyday-life facts, like the UV sunburn video, which got 33 shares from 698 views
Make short follow-ups to winners, such as clap switch part 3 or gyro on a drone, and test one English version since the only English video had decent YouTube views
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai? 🤔' titles with no surprise
Publishing videos on YouTube only, with no Instagram version
Niche component-spec topics (TDS, geophone, KY-038, CO2) without a relatable everyday hook
